classification.difficultyReason: Multiply independent outcome probabilities, account for the three possible positions of a single defect, and use all three defective as the complement of at most two.

content.prompt: A factory produces light bulbs, and 5% are faulty. Assume the bulbs in a random sample of 3 are independently faulty. Find the probability that

answer.worked:
Each bulb has probability $1-\frac1{20}=\frac{19}{20}$ of working.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{no defective bulbs})&=\left(\frac{19}{20}\right)^3\\P(\text{no defective bulbs})&=\frac{6859}{8000}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: exactly one light bulb is defective.

answer.worked:
The defective bulb can be first, second or third. All three orders have the same probability.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one defective bulb})&=3\times\frac1{20}\times\left(\frac{19}{20}\right)^2\\P(\text{exactly one defective bulb})&=\frac{1083}{8000}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: at most two light bulbs are defective.

answer.worked:
The complementary event is that all three bulbs are defective.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at most two defective bulbs})&=1-\left(\frac1{20}\right)^3\\P(\text{at most two defective bulbs})&=\frac{7999}{8000}.\end{align*}$$
